Definition: properly, salted (i.e. land), i.e. a desert
BiblicalUsage: Melechah is salt land, ground so salted that nothing grows there. Jeremiah 17:6 says the man who trusts in man shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited, and Job 39:6 makes the barren land the home of the wild ass.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe salt land is the picture of a life cut off from God: parched, empty, and unfit for dwelling.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
